paper_summary: Qu et al. (Kovove Mater. 61, 2023, 35-48) prepared Al-matrix syntactic foams by gravity infiltration casting of a cast Al-12.5Si-2.5Cu-1.2Mg alloy into packed beds of Al2O3 hollow spheres of three size ranges (0.5-1, 1-2, 2-3 mm), and studied the effect of sphere size and of homogenisation/ageing heat treatment on microstructure, quasi-static compressive properties (10^-3 1/s) and energy absorption. Foam density fell from 1.82 to 1.61 g/cm3 and porosity rose from 35.8 to 42.75 % as sphere size increased, while compressive strength, plateau strength and specific energy absorption all increased as sphere size decreased (as-cast 0.5-1 mm: 88.0 MPa, 66.55 MPa, 20.38 kJ/kg), attributed to the smaller lever torque on small spheres and their larger wall-thickness-to-diameter ratio. Heat treatment (515 C/1 h/AC being best) raised the plateau strength to 87.71 MPa and specific energy absorption to 30.45 kJ/kg, mainly through release of residual compressive stress around the spheres.

extraction_notes: PRIMARY DATA (7 records): all seven rows of Table 5 (three as-cast hollow-sphere size ranges 0.5-1, 1-2, 2-3 mm, and four heat-treatment conditions all using 0.5-1 mm spheres), joined with the matching density rows of Table 4 and the sphere geometry of Table 6. Note the text mislabels the tables in places: the properties table printed on p. 42 is headed 'Table 5' while the running text refers to it as 'Table 6', and the sphere geometry table is headed 'Table 6'. Unit conversions: densification strain converted from percent to fraction (52.76 % -> 0.5276 etc.); all strengths were already in MPa; densities already in g/cm3. particle_wall_thickness_ratio was converted from the paper's mean wall-thickness-to-radius ratio t/R to the schema's radius ratio eta = inner/outer radius = 1 - t/R, giving 0.903 (0.5-1 mm, t/R = 0.097), 0.905 (1-2 mm, 0.095) and 0.909 (2-3 mm, 0.091). Particle volume fraction is never reported and was left null; the paper's 'porosity' (35.8-42.8 %, from P = 1 - rho_sf/rho_matrix) is total porosity dominated by the hollow-sphere interiors, not unintended matrix voids, so it was recorded in microstructure_notes rather than in matrix_porosity_fraction. Test temperature was not stated (tests run 'in the atmosphere') and was recorded as 25 C; strain rate 10^-3 1/s; specimens 10 x 10 x 15 mm on a WDW3100 machine; no test standard is cited. Process route: gravity infiltration casting (melt at 750 C for 60 min into a packed bed heated to 500 C) has no matching enum value, so process_route = 'other' with the route named in matrix/microstructure notes; cure_or_process_temperature_c = 750 C (infiltration temperature). Schema has no field for specific energy absorption (kJ/kg) or energy absorption efficiency (%), so those Table 5 columns are lost: Es = 20.38, 19.53, 6.61 (as-cast 0.5-1, 1-2, 2-3 mm) and 30.45, 29.48, 27.51, 27.06 kJ/kg (heat treatments); efficiency = 81.23, 80.85, 80.17, 81.24, 89.40, 85.27, 87.39 %. No elastic modulus is reported anywhere. Table 1 (alumina hollow sphere data sheet) is badly garbled by the PDF extraction; the readable values are >99 % Al2O3 with Fe2O3 0.15 +/- 0.05, SiO2 0.2 +/- 0.1, Na2O 0.25 +/- 0.05 %, bulk (packed) density 0.5-1 g/cm3, supplied size 0.2-5 mm, application temperature 1800 C. Because 0.5-1 g/cm3 is a packed bulk density and not the particle true density, particle_true_density_g_cc was left null. SECONDARY DATA (18 records): Table 7 compares this work with published Al-matrix syntactic foams, giving only energy absorption capacity W (MJ/m3) and specific energy absorption Es (kJ/kg) plus synthesis method and matrix alloy; only W maps to the schema. Each row is recorded with data_origin = 'secondary' and the citation in sample_label. Filler type is NOT given in Table 7; where the cited reference title in the paper's own reference list names the filler unambiguously (cenospheres, Al2O3 hollow spheres, expanded perlite, expanded glass, pumice, expanded clay, bimodal ceramic microspheres) that was used, otherwise particle_type = 'other' with the detail in particle_grade, and confidence was set to 0.5-0.6 accordingly. Three Table 7 rows were deliberately excluded: the 'Present work' row (56.33 MJ/m3, 30.45 kJ/kg) because it duplicates the primary 515 C/1 h/AC record; the IFM/AFS row [57] (57.68 MJ/m3) because the cited work is an aluminium foam sandwich, not a syntactic foam; and the stirring-casting TiC-TiB2 reinforced Al row [59] (7.5 MJ/m3) because the cited work is an in-situ reinforced blown Al foam, not a hollow-particle composite.
